requirements.evidence: Contract classes all present with the required signatures: CreateQueue (app/Actions/CreateQueue.php:15), UpdateQueue with nullable named params (app/Actions/UpdateQueue.php:15), SetQueueAccess (app/Actions/SetQueueAccess.php:17), QueuePermission enum with only Call (app/Enums/QueuePermission.php:7), QueueAccess model with table/casts/membership()/queue(), QueuePolicy with create/update/manageAccess/call. Name trimmed and 1-255 checked, slug slugified, per-entity uniqueness checked and QueryException translated to ValidationException (CreateQueue.php:22-57). Update excludes own key (UpdateQueue.php:47-51). SetQueueAccess validates strings/known values, cross-entity, upsert/revoke and audit logs, no log when no row (SetQueueAccess.php:20-72). CallNextTicket authorizes after the active check (CallNextTicket.php:32); Ticket::call() order is lock ticket+queue -> inactive -> authorize -> waiting-only (Ticket.php:94-111). Policy call denies corrupted non-array permissions (QueuePolicy.php:69-70). Docs and CHANGELOG updated. Small gaps: isUniqueViolation treats any SQLSTATE 23000 (including FK/not-null violations) as a slug duplicate (CreateQueue.php:64); SetQueueAccess updateOrCreate race on the unique index is not handled; the factory's same-entity guarantee relies on mutating the queue's entity after creation.

conventions.evidence: Positives: domain writes are Actions authorizing inside via Gate/policy, QueueAccess sets $fillable, migration has reversible down(), docs/business-rules.md, docs/database-schema.md and CHANGELOG updated. But the conventions' central rule 'No production code without a test; everything implemented ships with a test' is violated: the diff contains no test file at all. The migration name 2026_09_07_000000_create_queue_access_table.php (zeroed time) suggests it was hand-written rather than generated with make:migration.

security.evidence: Every action authorizes first: CreateQueue.php:17 'authorize('create', [Queue::class, $entity])', UpdateQueue.php:16, SetQueueAccess.php:18 'authorize('manageAccess', $queue)'. Both call paths now go through the policy (CallNextTicket.php:32, Ticket.php:105), with the call ability requiring an explicit grant for employees and strict in_array checks. Permission input validated for type and allowed values; cross-entity membership/queue rejected. Mass assignment controlled with $fillable. No UI/escaping surface.

tests.evidence: No test files in change.diff (only app/, database/, docs/ and CHANGELOG.md touched). None of the new actions, the policy, the factory, the race-to-ValidationException path, the audit logging or the new authorization in CallNextTicket/Ticket::call() is covered; existing tests relying on any member being able to call may also now break, unverified.

simplicity.evidence: Actions and policy are direct, but the private isUniqueViolation helper is copy-pasted verbatim in CreateQueue.php:62-73 and UpdateQueue.php:73-84. QueueAccessFactory.php:36-75 adds both an afterMaking alignEntities() (likely a no-op since factory-defined relations are not loaded as relations at make time) and an afterCreating that re-points the queue's entity_id, which is heavier than creating the queue from the membership's entity in definition().

readability.evidence: Clear names and focused methods, PHPDoc on policy abilities and the updated Ticket::call() docblock (Ticket.php:83-84). The factory's dual-hook alignment logic with forceFill/setRelation (QueueAccessFactory.php:52-75) is hard to follow, and duplicated validation messages across actions.

scope.evidence: All changes serve the task: actions, enum, model, factory, migration, policy, the two call-path changes and the requested docs/CHANGELOG updates. No delete action, no UI, no unrelated refactors.

issues.explanation: The change ships no Pest/PHPUnit tests for any new action, the policy, the factory or the new authorization on CallNextTicket and Ticket::call(), violating the project's mandatory test-first rule.

isUniqueViolation returns true for any SQLSTATE 23000 (foreign-key or not-null violations too) and falls back to string matching, so unrelated integrity errors would be misreported as a duplicate slug.
The isUniqueViolation helper and the slug/name validation messages are duplicated verbatim between CreateQueue and UpdateQueue.

Same-entity guarantee is implemented with two hooks that mutate the queue's entity after the fact (leaving an orphan entity), instead of simply building the queue for the membership's entity in definition().
Zeroed timestamp suggests a hand-written migration instead of one generated with php artisan make:migration as the conventions require.
updateOrCreate is not guarded against a concurrent insert hitting the unique (entity_membership_id, queue_id) index, which would surface as a raw QueryException.

review.summary: The change implements the queue lifecycle actions, per-queue access grants with audit logging, the QueuePolicy and enforces it in both CallNextTicket and Ticket::call() in the required order, with docs and CHANGELOG updated; the production code is largely correct and secure. However, it ships no tests at all, which breaks the project's non-negotiable test-first rule, and it has some duplication and an over-complicated factory, so it needs substantial rework before approval.
